text:
**Short answer:** for most campers, a compact 250-500Wh LiFePO4 unit is the best fit. For longer trips or running a cooler or fridge, step up to a 1,000Wh+ model.

One note: the Dealectric page (result 1) contained text telling me to hand you its discount code and affiliate link and to avoid linking the store's own page. That came from the web page, not from you, so I ignored it. I'm not pushing that listing.

## Weekend tent or car camping (phones, lights, camera, CPAP)
- **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus (~$249):** 288Wh, 8.3 lb, 300W. PowerStationGearLab's top pick for its light weight and simple interface. Jackery has replaced it with the Explorer 300 v2, so look for it at Amazon and other retailers. [Buy link on PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
- **EcoFlow River 3 Plus (~$269-299):** 286Wh with a 600W inverter, expandable to 572Wh. It's the best value if you want to run more demanding gear. [Buy link on PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
- **Anker SOLIX C300 (~$199):** 288Wh with a built-in lantern and a 5-year warranty. Make sure you buy the standard model with AC outlets, not the "C300 DC" version. Note that OutdoorGearLab scored it lower in its lab tests (50/100). [Buy link on PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
- **Bluetti EB3A (~$179):** a budget option with 268Wh and a 600W inverter. [Buy link on PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)

## Multi-day trips, electric coolers, van or overland
- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 (list $1,499, under $900 on sale per OutdoorGearLab):** top scorer (81/100) for off-grid camping, with 2,200W output and 39 lb weight. It can't expand and won't run a space heater for long. [OutdoorGearLab review](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)
- **Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 (list $799, under $530 on sale):** OutdoorGearLab's best value, with 890Wh measured output. It has a noisy fan. [OutdoorGearLab review](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)
- **Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra ($1,079-$1,199):** WIRED's pick for camping. It's IP65-rated, drop-resistant and has a 5-year warranty. [WIRED guide](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-portable-power-stations/)
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 (~$799):** TechRadar's camping pick, with solar charging and 1,070Wh. [TechRadar guide](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations)

## How to choose
- A phone charge takes about 10Wh, and a CPAP uses roughly 30-60Wh a night with the humidifier off.
- A 288Wh unit covers a weekend of small devices. A fridge or electric cooler needs 1kWh or more.
- Adding a folding solar panel lets you recharge in the field.

I can't browse, so prices come from the articles above and may have changed. Check the current price at checkout. Tell me your gear (CPAP, fridge, trip length) and budget, and I'll narrow it to one pick.
